headings: Cancers in the Liver—A Significant Unmet Medical Need
Cancers in the Liver—Incidence and Mortality
Market Access and Commercial Clinical Adoption
paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to the "Company", "Delcath", "Delcath Systems", "we", "our", and "us" refers to Delcath Systems, Inc., a Delaware corporation, incorporated in August 1988, and all entities included in our consolidated financial statements. Our corporate offices are located at 566 Queensbury Avenue, Queensbury, New York 12804. Our telephone number is (518) 743-8892 and our internet address is www.delcath.com. The information found on, or otherwise accessible through, our website is not incorporated by reference into, and does not form a part of, this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We are an interventional oncology company focused on the treatment of cancers primary or metastatic to the liver. Our lead product, the HEPZATOTM KIT (melphalan for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System), a drug/device combination product ("HEPZATO" or "HEPZATO KIT"), was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (the "FDA") on August 14, 2023, indicated as a liver-directed treatment for adult patients with uveal melanoma with unresectable hepatic metastases affecting less than 50% of the liver and no extrahepatic disease, or extrahepatic disease limited to the bone, lymph nodes, subcutaneous tissues, or lung that is amenable to resection, or radiation. The first commercial use of the HEPZATO for the treatment of metastatic hepatic dominant uveal melanoma ("mUM") took place in January 2024.

In the United States, HEPZATO is considered a combination drug and device product and is regulated as a drug by the FDA. Primary jurisdiction for regulation of HEPZATO has been assigned to the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. The FDA has granted us six orphan drug designations (five for melphalan in the treatment of patients with ocular (uveal) melanoma, cutaneous melanoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and neuroendocrine tumor indications and one for doxorubicin in the treatment of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma).

We have sufficient raw material and component constituent parts of the HEPZATO KIT to meet anticipated demand and we intend to manage supply chain risk through stockpiled inventory and contracting with multiple suppliers for critical components.

In Europe, the hepatic delivery system is a stand-alone medical device having the same device components as HEPZATO, but without the melphalan hydrochloride and is approved for sale under the trade name CHEMOSAT Hepatic Delivery System for Melphalan, or CHEMOSAT, where it has been used at major medical centers to treat a wide range of cancers in the liver. On February 28, 2022, CHEMOSAT received Medical Device Regulation ("MDR") certification under the European Medical Devices Regulation (EU) 2017/745, which may be considered by jurisdictions when evaluating reimbursement. As of March 1, 2022, we assumed direct responsibility for sales, marketing and distribution of CHEMOSAT in Europe.
We operate as one operating segment. See Note 16 - "Segment Information" in the accompanying notes to our consolidated financial statements for further detail.

According to the American Cancer Society's ("ACS") Cancer Facts & Figures 2025 report, cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States, with more than 618,000 deaths and over 2 million new cases expected to be diagnosed in 2025. Cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, accounting for approximately 10 million deaths and 20 million new cases in 2022 according to GLOBOCAN, the database of the International Association of Cancer Registries. The financial burden of cancer is enormous for patients, their families and society. The liver is often the life-limiting organ for cancer patients and cancer that spreads to the liver is one of the leading causes of cancer death. Cancer that begins in one area of the body often metastasizes to the liver. Patient prognosis is generally poor once cancer has spread to the liver. Consequently, cancers in the liver remain a major unmet medical need globally.

Cancers in the liver consist of primary liver cancer and cancers metastatic to the liver. Primary liver cancers, hepatocellular carcinoma and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, originate in the liver or biliary tract and are particularly prevalent in populations where the primary risk factors for the disease, such as hepatitis-B, hepatitis-C, high levels of alcohol consumption, aflatoxin, cigarette smoking and exposure to industrial pollutants, are present. Cancers metastatic to the liver, also called liver metastasis, or secondary liver cancer, result from the spread or "metastases" of a primary cancer into the liver. These metastases often continue to grow even after the primary cancer in another part of the body has been removed or successfully treated. Given the vital biological functions of the liver, including processing nutrients from food and

filtering toxins from the blood, it is not uncommon for metastases to settle in the liver. In many cases patients die not as a result of their primary cancer, but from the tumors that metastasize to their liver. In the United States, metastatic liver disease is more prevalent than primary liver cancer. We estimate that the total potential addressable market for liver cancer (primary and metastatic) is approximately 200,000 in the United States per year. Based on industry reports, it is estimated the total addressable market ("TAM") in the United States for mUM, metastatic cholangiocarcinoma ("mCCA"), metastatic neuroendocrine tumor ("mNET"), metastatic colorectal cancer ("mCRC"), metastatic breast cancer ("mBC"), metastatic non-small cell lung cancer ("mNSCLC"), metastatic pancreatic cancer ("mPC") and HCC, is well over $1.0 billion.

Treatment of liver cancer is difficult. Current liver cancer treatment options include surgery, systemic treatment with anticancer drugs, and liver directed treatment options. Surgery options include surgical resection, liver transplant, and isolated hepatic perfusion ("IHP"). While surgical resection and liver transplant, when feasible, offer best possible outcomes for liver cancer patients, the percentage of patients that qualify for these procedures is low, generally 10% or less of the total liver cancer population. Clinical efficacy observed with IHP provided the rationale for using percutaneous hepatic profusion ("PHP") in mUM, as well as other tumor types, including colorectal cancer. Systemic options include systemic chemotherapy and immunotherapy agents. Minimally invasive options include external beam radiation therapy and liver directed procedures.

Procedures in the liver, and liver directed treatments (interventional oncology) are performed by an interventional radiologist. These procedures include trans-arterial chemoembolization (TACE, DEBTACE) and Radioembolization (SIRT, TARE, or Y90). We believe that CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO represent an important advancement in the potential liver-directed treatment of primary liver cancer and other cancers metastatic to the liver. Two key factors differentiate PHP with HEPZATO and CHEMOSAT from other liver directed therapies: the ability to treat the entire liver, including radiologically invisible micrometastases, and the repeatability of the procedure. We believe PHP with HEPZATO and CHEMOSAT is uniquely positioned either as a standalone therapy or as a complement to other therapies. In clinical studies with HEPZATO and CHEMOSAT, both treatment-naive and pretreated patients have benefited from the treatment, thus expanding the use to multiple lines of treatment.

Uveal melanoma frequently metastasizes to the liver. Based on third party research that we commissioned approximately 5,000-6,200 cases of uveal melanoma are diagnosed in the United States and Europe annually, and approximately 50% of these patients will develop metastatic disease. Of metastatic cases of uveal melanoma, approximately 90% of patients develop liver involvement. According to Lane et al., JAMA Ophthalmol. 2018 Sep 1;136(9):981-98, once uveal melanoma has spread to the liver, median overall survival for these patients is up to 12 months. There is no one standard of care for patients with uveal melanoma liver metastases. Based on our research, an estimated 800 patients with uveal melanoma liver metastases in the United States, and 1,200 patients in Europe may be eligible for treatment with HEPZATO or CHEMOSAT annually. Eligible patients are those with limited extrahepatic disease that can be treated with resection or radiation, who are able to safely undergo general anesthesia, and who have metastases involving less than 50% of the liver parenchyma. Currently 55% of the patients are not eligible for KIMMTRAK, the only approved uveal melanoma systemic therapy, and most patients are treated with multiple lines of therapy. We estimate the annual addressable market for this indication in the United States and Europe is approximately $600 million per year.

Colorectal cancer ("CRC") is one of the most prevalent cancers in the United States and Europe and has a high metastatic rate to the liver. GLOBOCAN 2022 estimates that there are 516,452 CRC diagnoses per year in the United States and the European Union. According to the ACS, in the United States there are approximately 160,186 diagnoses leading to 54,614 deaths.

Recent advances in the treatment of primary CRC have shown encouraging increases in 5-year survival; however, the presence of metastasis is an indicator for increased mortality probability. We estimate approximately 98,000 CRC patients in the United States, the United Kingdom and the European Union annually could be candidates for treatment with HEPZATO (if it received FDA approval for such treatment) and CHEMOSAT.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Financial Condition
We have incurred significant losses since inception and continuing losses may exhaust our capital resources.

We have in the past, and may in the future, become subject to litigation or claims arising in or outside the ordinary course of business that could negatively affect our business operations and financial condition.
We may be the subject of product liability claims or product recalls, and we may be unable to maintain insurance adequate to cover potential liabilities.
Risks Related to Manufacturing, Commercialization and Market Acceptance of CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO
If we cannot successfully manufacture CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO, our ability to develop and commercialize the system would be impaired.
We do not have written contracts with all of our suppliers for the manufacture of components for CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO.
We may be unsuccessful in commercializing CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO because of inadequate infrastructure or an ineffective commercialization strategy.
We may need to enter into collaborative arrangements with third parties to help market and sell CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO, but it may not be successful.
If we fail to overcome the challenges inherent in international operations, our business and results of operations may be materially adversely affected.
Rapid technological developments in treatment methods for liver cancer and competition with other forms of liver cancer treatments could affect our ability to achieve meaningful revenues or profit.
Risks Related to FDA and Foreign Regulatory Approvals and Regulatory Matters
Our ability to market HEPZATO is limited to those uses that are approved.
If future clinical trials are unsuccessful, significantly delayed or not completed, we may not be able to market HEPZATO for other indications.

We are subject to significant ongoing regulatory obligations and oversight in the European Union and the United States and will be in any other country where we receive marketing authorization or approval.

These risks include those described below and may include additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial. If any of the events or circumstances described in the following risk factors occur, our business operations, performance, financial condition and prospects could be materially and adversely affected and the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. We cannot assure you that any of the events discussed below will not occur.

As of December 31, 2025, we had $43.5 million in cash and cash equivalents and $47.6 million in short-term investments. We have a substantial accumulated deficit and recurring operating losses in prior years. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we incurred a net gain of approximately $2.7 million and a net loss of $26.4 million, respectively, and notwithstanding any prior net gain, we may continue to incur losses in the future. To date, we have funded our operations primarily through a combination of private placements and public offerings of our securities and debt financing, including convertible notes, as well as from revenue we have generated from HEPZATO and CHEMOSAT. If we continue to incur losses, we may exhaust our capital resources, and as a result may be unable to further commercialize our products in the United States and the European Union and any other jurisdictions where we may receive regulatory approval for our products or conduct future product development, if any, including clinical trials for new product candidates or for HEPZATO or CHEMOSAT in additional indications for which we do not currently have regulatory approval.

Our prior losses and potential future losses have had and would continue to have an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital. Our ability to generate additional product revenue from HEPZATO and CHEMOSAT, for any currently approved indications or any indications for which they are approved in the future, or future product candidates, if any, also depends on a number of additional factors, including, but not limited to, our ability to:
•successfully commercialize and sell HEPZATO and CHEMOSAT pursuant to existing regulatory approvals;

•successfully complete research and clinical development of future product candidates, if any, including clinical trials for new product candidates or for HEPZATO or CHEMOSAT in additional indications for which we do not currently have regulatory approval, and obtain regulatory approval for those product candidates and indications, as applicable;

•establish and maintain supply and manufacturing relationships, under commercially reasonable terms, with third parties, and ensure adequate, scaled up and legally compliant manufacturing of necessary components, including melphalan, bulk drug substances, drug products, and those used to manufacture the medical device, to maintain sufficient supply;

disease limited to the bone, lymph nodes, subcutaneous tissues, or lung that is amenable to resection, or radiation. The first commercial use of the HEPZATO KIT for the treatment of mUM took place in January 2024.

In the United States, HEPZATO is considered a combination drug and device product and is regulated as a drug by the FDA. Primary jurisdiction for regulation of HEPZATO has been assigned to the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. The FDA has granted us six orphan drug designations (five for melphalan in the treatment of patients with ocular (uveal) melanoma, cutaneous melanoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and neuroendocrine tumor indications and one for doxorubicin in the treatment of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma).

We have sufficient raw material and component constituent parts of the HEPZATO KIT to meet anticipated demand and we intend to manage supply chain risk through stockpiled inventory and contracting with multiple suppliers for critical components.

In Europe, the hepatic delivery system is a stand-alone medical device having the same device components as HEPZATO, but without the melphalan hydrochloride and is approved for sale under the trade name CHEMOSAT Hepatic Delivery System for Melphalan, or CHEMOSAT, where it has been used at major medical centers to treat a wide range of cancers in the liver. On February 28, 2022, CHEMOSAT received MDR certification under the European Medical Devices Regulation (EU) 2017/745, which may be considered by jurisdictions when evaluating reimbursement. As of March 1, 2022, we have assumed direct responsibility for sales, marketing and distribution of CHEMOSAT in Europe.

Our clinical development program for HEPZATO was comprised of the FOCUS Trial, a global registration clinical trial that investigated objective response rate in patients with mUM. The current focus of our clinical development program is to generate clinical data for CHEMOSAT and HEPZATO in patients with mUM, either as monotherapy or in combination with immunotherapy. On May 6, 2024, we announced the publication of results from our Phase 3 FOCUS Trial, including an ORR of 36.3%, which included 7.7% of patients with Complete Response, as determined by an Independent Review Committee. An ORR of 36.3% in the FOCUS study was statistically significantly better than the pooled ORR estimate (a weighted mean of the observed ORR) of 5.5% in the historical control group. We expect that the publication will support increased clinical adoption of and reimbursement for CHEMOSAT in Europe, and support reimbursement in various jurisdictions, including the United States.

In addition to HEPZATO's use to treat mUM, the Company believes that HEPZATO has the potential to treat other cancers in the liver, such as metastatic colorectal cancer, metastatic breast cancer, metastatic neuroendocrine tumors and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

Our IND application for a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating HEPZATO in combination with SOC for liver-dominant mCRC was cleared by the FDA in December 2024. The Phase 2 trial will evaluate the safety and efficacy of HEPZATO in combination with trifluridine-tipiracil and bevacizumab compared to trifluridine-tipiracil and bevacizumab alone in patients with liver-dominant mCRC receiving third-line treatment. Approximately 90 patients will be enrolled in this randomized, controlled trial. Patient enrollment began during the third quarter of 2025, with the study expected to take place at more than 20 sites across the United States and Europe. In July 2025, we received authorization from the European Union and United Kingdom regulatory authorities for the clinical study of Melphalan for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System in patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer with the liver dominant disease. The trial's primary endpoint, hPFS, is anticipated to read out by the end of 2027, while OS, a secondary endpoint, is expected in 2028. We estimate that the total addressable market ("TAM") for liver-dominant mCRC receiving third-line treatment is between 6,000 and 10,000 patients annually in the United States. This market includes patients who present with significant liver disease burden, with liver-dominant status determined through radiological and clinical criteria. By targeting this patient population, we aim to provide a novel treatment option for those with limited therapeutic alternatives.

On April 28, 2025, we announced our IND application clearance by the FDA for the Phase 2 clinical trial of HEPZATO in mBC. The Phase 2 trial will evaluate the safety and efficacy of HEPZATO in combination with SOC versus SOC alone in patients with liver-dominant HER2-negative mBC following the failure of previous treatments. The SOC options will be the physician's choice of eribulin, vinorelbine or capecitabine. We expect approximately 90 patients will be enrolled in this randomized, controlled trial. The study will take place at more than 15 sites across the United States and Europe, with patient enrollment expected to begin in the first quarter of 2026. The trial's primary endpoint, hPFS, is anticipated to read out by the end of 2028, while results for OS, a secondary endpoint, is expected in 2029.

We estimate that approximately 7,000 patients annually in the United States are affected by HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with liver metastases and are candidates for third line treatment. This population includes patients with a significant burden of liver metastases, which are likely to be the primary cause of mortality. By focusing on this demographic, we intend to offer a novel therapeutic option to those patients with limited treatment alternatives.
We believe that these and similar disease states are areas of unmet medical needs that represent significant market opportunities.

We expense research and development costs as they are incurred. We expect our research and development expenses to increase for the foreseeable future relating to the costs required to complete these Phase 2 clinical trials.

paragraphs: 我們為一介入性腫瘤學公司，專注於治療原發或轉移至肝臟之癌症。我們之主要產品為 HEPZATOTM KIT（melphalan for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System），為一藥物/醫療器材組合產品（"HEPZATO" 或 "HEPZATO KIT"），於2023年8月14日經美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，用於治療成人患者之眼葡萄膜黑色素瘤，其肝臟轉移病竈佔肝臟總體積少於50% 且無其他肝外病變，或肝外病變僅限於骨骼、淋巴結、皮下組織或肺部且可進行手術切除或放射治療。HEPZATO 用於治療轉移性肝臟優勢眼葡萄膜黑色素瘤（"mUM"）之首例商業使用於2024年1月進行。
於美國，HEPZATO 被視為藥物與醫療器材組合產品，並由FDA 視為藥物進行管理。HEPZATO 之主要監管權限已歸屬於FDA 之藥物評估與研究中心。FDA 已授予我們六項罕見疾病藥物指定（五項為melphalan 用於治療眼葡萄膜黑色素瘤、皮膚黑色素瘤、肝內膽管癌、肝細胞癌及神經內分泌腫瘤之適應症，以及一項為doxorubicin 用於治療肝細胞癌之適應症）。
我們擁有足夠之原料及零組件以應對預期之需求，我們意圖透過存貨儲備及與多個供應商簽訂契約以管理供應鏈風險。

於歐洲，肝臟給藥系統為一獨立之醫療器材，其組成零組件與HEPZATO 相同，但不包含melphalan hydrochloride，並以CHEMOSAT Hepatic Delivery System for Melphalan 或 CHEMOSAT 之商標核准銷售，已於主要醫療中心用以治療肝臟之多種癌症。於2022年2月28日，CHEMOSAT 已取得醫療器材法規（"MDR"）認證，依據歐洲醫療器材法規（EU）2017/745，此認證可能被各司法管轄區用以評估費用報銷。自2022年3月1日起，我們已直接負責CHEMOSAT 在歐洲之銷售、行銷與分銷。
我們僅運作一個營運分部。有關更多細節，請參閱附註16 - "分部資訊" 之相關說明。

根據美國癌症協會（"ACS"）之《2025年癌症事實與數據》報告，癌症為美國第二大死因，預計2025年將有超過618,000 人死亡，並診斷出超過200萬例新病例。癌症為全球主要死因之一，根據國際癌症登記協會之GLOBOCAN數據庫，2022年約有1000萬人死亡，並診斷出2000萬例新病例。癌症對患者、其家屬及社會而言，財務負擔極為沉重。肝臟常為癌症患者之生命限制器官，而轉移至肝臟之癌症為癌症死亡之主要原因之一。癌症常自身體某一區域擴散至肝臟。一旦癌症擴散至肝臟，患者預後通常不佳。因此，肝臟癌症仍為全球未滿足之重大醫療需求。

肝臟癌症包含原發性肝臟癌症及轉移至肝臟之癌症。原發性肝臟癌症，如肝細胞癌及肝內膽管癌，源自肝臟或膽道，尤其在具有疾病主要風險因素之人羣中更為普遍，如乙型肝炎、丙型肝炎、高酒精攝取量、黃曲毒素、吸煙及工業污染物暴露。轉移至肝臟之癌症，亦稱為肝臟轉移，或稱為次發性肝臟癌症，係因原發癌症擴散至肝臟所致。這些轉移常在原發癌症於身體其他部位已被切除或成功治療後，仍持續生長。考慮到肝臟之重要生物功能，包括處理食物中之營養物質，

過濾血液中的毒素，肝臟常是轉移性腫瘤的常見定居地。許多患者並非因原發癌症而死亡，而是因轉移至肝臟的腫瘤所致。在美國，轉移性肝臟疾病比原發性肝癌更為普遍。我們估計，肝癌（包括原發性和轉移性）在美國的年潛在可達市場約為 200,000 例。根據產業報告，美國 mUM、轉移性膽管癌（mCCA）、轉移性神經內分泌瘤（mNET）、轉移性結腸直腸癌（mCRC）、轉移性乳癌（mBC）、轉移性非小細胞肺癌（mNSCLC）、轉移性胰臟癌（mPC）及肝細胞癌（HCC）的總可達市場（"TAM"）超過 1.0 十億美元。

肝癌的治療困難。目前肝癌治療選項包括手術、系統性治療使用抗癌藥物，以及針對肝臟的治療選項。手術選項包括手術切除、肝臟移植及隔離肝臟灌注（"IHP"）。雖然手術切除和肝臟移植在可行的情況下，為肝癌患者提供最佳治療結果，但符合這些手術條件的患者比例通常低於總肝癌患者數的 10% 或更低。隔離肝臟灌注（IHP）觀察到的臨牀效果，為在 mUM 以及其他腫瘤類型（包括結腸癌）中使用經皮肝臟灌注（"PHP"）提供了理論基礎。系統性選項包括系統性化療和免疫治療藥物。微創選項包括外照射放射治療和針對肝臟的程序。

肝臟手術及針對肝臟的治療（介入放射學）由介入放射科醫師執行。這些程序包括經動脈化療栓塞（TACE, DEBTACE）及放射栓塞（SIRT, TARE, 或 Y90）。我們認為 CHEMOSAT 和 HEPZATO 在潛在針對肝臟的治療（包括原發性肝癌及其他轉移至肝臟的癌症）中代表重要的進步。PHP 與 HEPZATO 和 CHEMOSAT 相較於其他針對肝臟的治療方式，有兩個關鍵區別：能夠治療整個肝臟，包括放射學上無法看見的微轉移病竈，以及程序的可重複性。我們認為 PHP 與 HEPZATO 和 CHEMOSAT 在作為單獨治療或與其他治療方式配合使用時，具有獨特的優勢。在 HEPZATO 和 CHEMOSAT 的臨牀研究中，無論是未曾接受治療或已接受治療的患者，都從治療中受益，因此擴展了治療線路的應用。

視網膜黑色素瘤常轉移至肝臟。根據我們委託第三方研究的資料，美國和歐洲每年約診斷出 5,000 至 6,200 例視網膜黑色素瘤，約有 50% 的患者會發展出轉移性疾病。在視網膜黑色素瘤的轉移病例中，約有 90% 的患者會出現肝臟受累。根據 Lane 等人，JAMA Ophthalmol. 2018 年 9 月 1 日；136(9):981-98，一旦視網膜黑色素瘤轉移到肝臟，這些患者的中位總體存活時間為至多 12 個月。目前尚無針對視網膜黑色素瘤肝臟轉移患者的標準治療方式。根據我們的研究，美國約有 800 例、歐洲約有 1,200 例視網膜黑色素瘤肝臟轉移患者每年可能符合接受 HEPZATO 或 CHEMOSAT 治療的條件。符合條件的患者為那些有有限的肝外疾病且可接受切除或放射治療、能夠安全接受全身麻醉，且轉移病竈佔肝臟組織少於 50% 的患者。目前 55% 的患者不符合 KIMMTRAK（唯一核准的視網膜黑色素瘤系統性治療）的治療條件，而大多數患者接受多線治療。我們估計美國和歐洲此適應症的年可達市場約為 600 百萬美元。
結腸直腸癌（"CRC"）是美國和歐洲最常見的癌症之一，且有高比例的轉移至肝臟。GLOBOCAN 2022 估計美國和歐盟每年診斷出 516,452 例 CRC。根據美國癌症協會（ACS），美國每年約有 160,186 例診斷導致 54,614 例死亡。
近期在原發性 CRC 治療方面的進展顯示，5 年存活率有令人鼓舞的提升；然而，轉移的出現是增加死亡風險的指標。我們估計，美國、英國和歐盟每年約有 98,000 例 CRC 患者可能符合接受 HEPZATO（若獲得 FDA 批准用於此治療）和 CHEMOSAT 治療的條件。
以下關於我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論，應與本年度10-K表報中所列之合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。

本公司為專注於治療原發或轉移至肝臟之癌症之介入性腫瘤治療公司。我們的主打產品為HEPZATO KIT（melphalan for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System），為一種藥物/醫療器材組合產品，於2023年8月14日獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准，用於治療成人患有無法手術切除之肝臟轉移性眼黑色素瘤，且影響肝臟小於50%且無肝外疾病，或肝外疾病限於骨骼、淋巴結、皮下組織或肺部且可手術切除或接受放射治療之患者。
HEPZATO KIT用於治療mUM（metastatic uveal melanoma）之首例商業應用於2024年1月進行。
在美國，HEPZATO被視為一種藥物與醫療器材組合產品，並由FDA作為藥物進行管理。HEPZATO之主要監管權限已歸屬FDA藥物評估與研究中心。FDA已授予我們六項罕見疾病藥物認定（其中五項為melphalan用於治療患有眼（uveal）黑色素瘤、皮膚黑色素瘤、肝內膽管癌、肝細胞癌及神經內分泌腫瘤之患者，以及一項為doxorubicin用於治療肝細胞癌之患者）。
我們擁有足夠之原料及HEPZATO KIT零組件以應對預期之需求，並計畫透過存貨儲備及與多個供應商簽訂契約以管理供應鏈風險。

在歐洲，肝臟給藥系統為一種獨立之醫療器材，其組成元件與HEPZATO相同，但不包含melphalan hydrochloride，並以CHEMOSAT Hepatic Delivery System for Melphalan（或簡稱CHEMOSAT）之名稱獲准銷售。該產品已在主要醫療中心用於治療肝臟多種癌症。2022年2月28日，CHEMOSAT已取得根據歐洲醫療器材法規（EU）2017/745之MDR認證，此認證可能被各司法管轄區用以評估補償事宜。自2022年3月1日起，本公司已直接負責CHEMOSAT在歐洲之銷售、行銷與分銷。

HEPZATO之臨牀發展計畫包含FOCUS試驗，為一全球性註冊臨牀試驗，用以評估對mUM患者之客觀反應率。目前本公司臨牀發展計畫之重點為產生針對mUM患者之CHEMOSAT與HEPZATO之臨牀數據，無論是單獨使用或與免疫治療組合使用。2024年5月6日，本公司宣佈FOCUS試驗之第三期結果已發表，包含36.3%之客觀反應率（ORR），其中7.7%之患者經獨立審查委員會判定為完全反應。FOCUS試驗中36.3%之ORR在統計上顯著優於歷史對照組之加權平均ORR估計值（5.5%）。我們預期此發表將支持CHEMOSAT在歐洲之臨牀採用與補償，並支持各司法管轄區（包括美國）之補償。
除了HEPZATO用於治療mUM之外，本公司認為HEPZATO有潛力用於治療其他肝臟癌症，例如轉移性結腸癌、轉移性乳癌、轉移性神經內分泌腫瘤及肝內膽管癌。

本公司於2024年12月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准IND申請，用以進行HEPZATO與標準療法（SOC）聯合治療肝轉移性結直腸癌（mCRC）之第二期臨牀試驗。第二期試驗將評估HEPZATO與三氟尿苷-替匹拉辛及貝伐珠單抗聯合治療，與單獨使用三氟尿苷-替匹拉辛及貝伐珠單抗在肝轉移性結直腸癌患者接受第三線治療時之安全性與有效性。預計約90名患者將參與此隨機控制試驗。患者入組於2025年第三季開始，試驗預計於美國與歐洲超過20個試驗點進行。2025年7月，本公司獲歐盟與英國監管當局核准進行Melphalan for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System於難治性轉移性結直腸癌（肝轉移）患者的臨牀試驗。試驗主要評估指標hPFS預計於2027年底揭曉，次要評估指標OS預計於2028年揭曉。本公司估計，美國接受第三線治療之肝轉移性結直腸癌患者之總可達市場（"TAM"）每年約為6,000至10,000名患者。此市場包含具顯著肝病負擔之患者，其肝轉移性狀態經放射學與臨牀標準判定。透過針對此患者族羣，本公司旨在為那些治療選擇有限之患者提供創新治療選項。

本公司於2025年4月28日宣佈，已獲FDA核准IND申請，用以進行HEPZATO於HER2陰性轉移性乳癌（mBC）之第二期臨牀試驗。第二期試驗將評估HEPZATO與標準療法（SOC）聯合治療，與單獨使用標準療法（SOC）在HER2陰性轉移性乳癌患者接受第三線治療時之安全性與有效性。標準療法（SOC）選項為醫師選擇之eribulin、vinorelbine或capecitabine。預計約90名患者將參與此隨機控制試驗。試驗預計於美國與歐洲超過15個試驗點進行，患者入組預計於2026年第一季開始。試驗主要評估指標hPFS預計於2028年底揭曉，次要評估指標OS結果預計於2029年揭曉。
本公司估計，美國每年約有7,000名患者患有HER2陰性轉移性乳癌伴隨肝轉移，並為第三線治療之候選者。此族羣包含具有顯著肝轉移負擔之患者，這些轉移可能為主要致死原因。透過聚焦此族羣，本公司旨在為那些治療選擇有限之患者提供創新治療選項。
本公司認為這些及類似疾病狀態為未滿足之醫療需求領域，代表重要的市場機會。
本公司於發生時即將研究與開發費用計入費用。本公司預期未來一段時間內，研究與開發費用將因完成這些第二期臨牀試驗所需成本而增加。
本公司預期之研究與開發費用將主要由：

headings: 與本公司業務及財務狀況相關之風險
自設立以來，本公司已產生重大虧損，且持續虧損可能耗盡本公司之資金資源。
過往本公司曾並可能於未來因業務或非業務常規事項而成為訴訟或聲請之對象，此等情形可能對本公司之業務運作及財務狀況產生負面影響。
本公司可能成為產品責任聲請或產品回收之對象，且本公司可能無法維持足夠之保險以覆蓋潛在之責任。
與CHEMOSAT及HEPZATO之製造、商業化及市場接受度相關之風險
若本公司無法成功製造CHEMOSAT及HEPZATO，將影響本公司開發及商業化系統之能力。
本公司對於CHEMOSAT及HEPZATO之零組件製造供應商並未與所有供應商簽訂書面契約。
本公司可能因基礎設施不足或商業化策略不當而無法成功商業化CHEMOSAT及HEPZATO。
我們可能需要與第三方合作，以協助行銷與銷售 CHEMOSAT 和 HEPZATO，但這可能不會成功。
若我們無法克服國際營運中固有的挑戰，將可能對我們的業務及營運結果造成重大不利影響。
肝癌治療方法的技術快速發展與其他肝癌治療方式的競爭，可能影響我們實現有意義收入或獲利的能力。
與美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）及外國監管核准與監管事項相關的風險
我們行銷 HEPZATO 的能力僅限於已核准的用途。
若未來臨牀試驗未成功、大幅延遲或未完成，我們可能無法為其他適應症行銷 HEPZATO。
我們在歐盟及美國面臨重大持續的監管義務與監督，並在任何我們取得行銷許可或核准的國家皆然。

本公司過去的虧損與潛在未來虧損已對股東權益與營運資金造成不利影響，且未來仍將持續造成不利影響。本公司能否從HEPZATO與CHEMOSAT產生更多產品收入，無論是目前核准的適應症或未來核准的適應症，或未來產品候選藥物，若有的話，還取決於許多其他因素，包括但不限於本公司能否：
•根據現有監管核准成功商業化並銷售HEPZATO與CHEMOSAT；
•成功完成未來產品候選藥物的研究與臨牀開發，包括新產品候選藥物或HEPZATO或CHEMOSAT在其他適應症的臨牀試驗，若尚未獲得目前核准，並取得這些產品候選藥物與適應症的監管核准，如適用；
•與第三方建立並維持供應與製造關係，在商業合理條款下，並確保必要零組件，包括甲基苯肼、原料藥、藥品製劑及用以製造醫療器材的零組件，的充足、擴充規模且符合法律的製造，以維持足夠供應；
